title: Fenner Insurance Agency, Inc. - Marchfield
description: The website of an independent insurance agency on Bellamy Street in Marchfield: nine template pages about types of insurance, staff photographs described but not shown, a quote form that goes nowhere, and a syndicated safety-tip feed that stopped in July 2014.

blocks.text: *** OFFICE CLOSED THURSDAY 28 NOVEMBER AND FRIDAY 29 NOVEMBER *** ASK US ABOUT BUNDLING YOUR AUTO AND HOME *** OUR 52nd YEAR IN MARCHFIELD ***

blocks.body:
Welcome to the online home of [b]Fenner Insurance Agency, Inc.[/b]

As an independent insurance agency, we are not owned by any one insurance company. We represent nine of them. That means we can place your policy where it fits instead of where we are told to put it, and it means that when a company raises its rates or stops writing in this county, you do not have to start over with a stranger.

We have been doing this in Marchfield since 1961 and in Gridfall since 2009.

[b]Marchfield office:[/b] 31 Bellamy Street, Marchfield. Telephone [b]744-1195[/b]. Monday to Friday, 8:30 to 4:30.

[b]Gridfall office:[/b] 141 Mill Street, Gridfall. Telephone [b]782-2262[/b]. Monday and Thursday, 9:00 to 3:00.

If nobody answers in Gridfall it is because it is a Tuesday. Ring Marchfield.

items: [url=/auto]Auto insurance[/url] -- cars, light trucks, motorcycles, the third vehicle that does not run.
[url=/home]Homeowners insurance[/url] -- and dwelling fire for the rentals.
[url=/farm]Farm insurance[/url] -- farm owners, equipment, liability, crop and hail through Midstate.
[url=/business]Business insurance[/url] -- shops, contractors, churches, halls, two fire companies.
[url=/life]Life insurance[/url] -- term, whole life, final expense.
[url=/recreational]Recreational vehicles[/url] -- campers, trailers, the boat that is on the trailer.

[url=/claims]Report a claim[/url] -- every company's 24-hour number, on one page. Print it and put it in the glove box.

[b]Latest article:[/b] [i]Grilling Safety: Five Things To Check Before You Light[/i] -- posted 7 July 2014. [url=/news]Read more agency news and safety tips[/url].

The counter came with the template and was reset in 2018 when Delbrook moved their servers, so it is nine thousand of something and not nine thousand people.

[i]Copyright 2013 Fenner Insurance Agency, Inc. All rights reserved. Site design by Delbrook Marketing Services. Site last updated: 08/04/2014.[/i]

At Fenner Insurance Agency, Inc., we believe that insurance is a relationship and not a transaction. Our licensed professionals take the time to understand your needs, review your existing coverage, and recommend solutions tailored to your situation. We are proud to serve the families and businesses of Verity County.

As an independent agency we represent multiple insurance carriers, which allows us to shop the market on your behalf at each renewal.

[i]The two paragraphs above came with the website. They are not wrong. They are just not how anybody here talks. -- D.F.H.[/i]

A man comes in because he bought a truck on Saturday and it has to be insured before he drives it Monday. That is most of this job. The rest is renewals, certificates for contractors who need one by four o'clock, and sitting across a desk from somebody whose house has water in it.

We are nine companies deep and we know which of them pays a hail claim without an argument and which of them will send an adjuster from three counties away and take eleven days about it. That knowledge is not written down anywhere and it is the entire reason to use an agent instead of a website.

I am the third Fenner in this office and there will not be a fourth, and that is fine. My son teaches. -- [b]Dee Fenner Hoke[/b]

head: YEAR
WHAT
rows: Russell J. Fenner opens an office in a room above the hardware on Bellamy Street. One company, personal auto, and a rented adding machine.
First farm appointment, Pell Valley Mutual. Still our largest company.
Moved across and down to 31 Bellamy Street, where we still are.

The fire at the Blue Kestrel. Kitchen, eleven days shut. The claim was paid and it was not paid quickly, and we have heard about that at every chicken supper since. Russ said at the time that he would have been slow too with those receipts, which did not help.
Gerald "Jerry" Fenner joins his father. Licensed the same year.
Delores Fenner joins the office. Filing, then rating, then a licence in 1989.
Russell Fenner dies in March. Jerry takes the agency.

The flood. Three hundred and twelve claims in the nine days after 7 March, most of them in Gridfall. Bellamy Street had no telephone service for two of those days and we worked out of the town hall with a legal pad. See Tom Norris's [url=synth://tnorris.verity.net/flood]account of the flood[/url], which is better than ours.
Last year we put the agency name on a softball shirt. Sandy Reber picked the team up the following spring and has had it since.
First rating computer. It took a week to learn and saved four hours a day.
The June outage in Gridfall. Forty-one claims through this office.
Jerry retires. He keeps renewing his licence every two years and has not explained why.
Gridfall office opens at 141 Mill Street, in what was Kerchner Jewelers. Two days a week.
Tyler Frantz joins and is licensed in November.

Whatever you need to protect, Fenner Insurance Agency, Inc. has a solution. Select a coverage type below to learn more about how we can help you and your family in Marchfield and throughout Verity County.

These nine pages came with the website package. Four of them are for things this office writes twice a year. We asked for a farm page that talked about hail and we got the one below, which is about a barn in a state we are not in.

If you want to know whether we can write something, telephone and ask. The answer is usually yes and it takes ninety seconds. -- [b]D.F.H.[/b]

Your automobile is more than a means of transportation. It is your commute, your freedom, and for many households the second largest purchase they will ever make. The right auto insurance policy protects that investment and protects you from the financial consequences of an accident.

At Fenner Insurance Agency, Inc. we review your driving habits, your vehicles and your household to build a policy that fits. We represent multiple carriers, so if your rate moves at renewal we can shop it without you having to start again somewhere else.

items: Bodily injury and property damage liability
Classic and antique vehicle policies on agreed value

blocks.body: Many drivers carry only the state minimum limits of liability, which have not been raised in many years and which can be exhausted by a single emergency room visit. A review takes fifteen minutes and often costs less than you expect.

[i]Two practical things this page does not say. One: the minimum limits will not cover a three car accident on a wet morning and they never did. Two: if you are adding a sixteen year old, ring us before you buy the car and not after. The car matters more than the driver does to the rate and nobody believes that until they see the two numbers. -- T.F., 2013[/i]
Contact a licensed agent at Fenner Insurance Agency, Inc. today for a no-obligation review of your current coverage. [url=/quote]Request your free quote online[/url] or telephone our office.

Your home is where your life happens. It is also, for most families, their single largest asset. A homeowners policy from Fenner Insurance Agency, Inc. protects the structure, the contents, and your liability to others, and it does it at a price we will review with you every year whether you ask us to or not.

We write homeowners through several carriers, including companies that understand older houses, wood heat and outbuildings, which not every company does.

items: Personal property, at replacement cost where available
Loss of use and additional living expense
Personal liability and medical payments to others
Scheduled items -- rings, guns, tools, tack, instruments
Service line and equipment breakdown endorsements
Ordinance or law coverage on older construction

blocks.body: Building costs rise. A policy written ten years ago may insure your house for considerably less than it would cost to rebuild it today, and the shortfall does not appear until the day it matters.

[i]Three things we get asked every week and none of them are on this page.

A standard homeowners policy does not cover flood. Not from the creek, not from the road, not from water coming in at the foundation. See the [url=/flood]flood page[/url].

Food spoiled in a power outage is usually covered and usually capped at $500, and there is a deductible in front of it. See the [url=/faq]questions page[/url] for what happened here in June 2003.

A wood stove is not a problem. A wood stove that the company does not know about is a problem. Tell us and we will get it inspected and written properly. -- D.F.H.[/i]
Contact a licensed agent at Fenner Insurance Agency, Inc. today for a no-obligation review of your current coverage. [url=/quote]Request your free quote online[/url] or telephone our office.

The family farm faces risks that a homeowners policy was never designed to address. From the farmhouse to the machine shed, from livestock to liability arising out of farming operations, a farm owners policy brings your exposures together under one program.

Fenner Insurance Agency, Inc. has written farm business in this area since 1968 and understands the seasonal nature of agricultural operations.

items: Barns, machine sheds, grain bins, fencing
Scheduled and blanket farm personal property
Farm machinery, including equipment in transit
Livestock, including collision and named perils
Farm liability and custom farming liability
Crop and hail through Midstate Crop & Hail

blocks.body: Coverage for the modern farm should be reviewed each year before planting season. Equipment values, acreage and hired labour all change, and a policy that fit last spring may not fit this one.

[i]Hail dates in this county: the deadline for crop and hail is usually the end of the first week in June and it moves. Ring us in May.

Also: if you have started renting ground to somebody, or taken on custom work for a neighbour, that is a different policy from the one you have. This is the single most common gap we find, and we find it after the fact more often than before it. -- D.F.H.[/i]
The [url=synth://marchfield-coop.com/]Marchfield Farmers Cooperative[/url] posts the grain bids and the agronomy calendar, and is a better guide to when anything is happening than we are.
Contact a licensed agent at Fenner Insurance Agency, Inc. today for a no-obligation review of your current coverage. [url=/quote]Request your free quote online[/url] or telephone our office.

You have built your business. Protecting it should not be complicated. A business owners policy brings property, liability and business interruption together in a single package designed for small and mid-sized operations.

Whether you own a retail storefront, operate as a contractor, or manage a not-for-profit organisation, the licensed professionals at Fenner Insurance Agency, Inc. can help you identify and address your exposures.

items: Commercial auto, including hired and non-owned
Directors and officers liability for boards and non-profits
Surety and performance bonds through Cardiff
Workers compensation placed with the state fund

blocks.body: Many small business owners assume their homeowners policy covers business equipment kept at home. In most cases it does not, or covers it only to a small sublimit. Call our office in {{city}} to schedule a review.

[i]What we actually write in this county: seventeen Mill Street and Bellamy Street storefronts, thirty-one contractors, nine churches, four fire halls, two volunteer fire companies, a lodge, a bowling alley, and the fairground's liability for the week of the fair.

If you need a certificate of insurance, ring and ask for one. They are free, they take four minutes, and the general contractor is not going to let you on the job without one. Do not fax us the request the morning you need it and then also ring; we will do the same thing twice. -- G.W.[/i]
Contact a licensed agent at Fenner Insurance Agency, Inc. today for a no-obligation review of your current coverage. [url=/quote]Request your free quote online[/url] or telephone our office.

Life insurance is not about you. It is about the people who depend on you, and about what their lives look like on the worst day of them.

The agents at Fenner Insurance Agency, Inc. will sit down with you and work out how much coverage your family actually needs, for how long, and what it will cost. There is no obligation and there is no pressure.

items: Key person and buy-sell coverage for businesses

blocks.body: A healthy person in their thirties can often insure themselves for a quarter of a million dollars for less than the cost of a mobile telephone plan. Speak with a licensed agent today at {{agency_phone}}.

[i]We write life. We are not going to telephone you about it at supper time and we are not going to send you a letter that looks like a bill. If you want it, come in.

One thing worth saying plainly: a burial policy is not a bad product and it is not an investment. If somebody is selling you one as an investment, that is the part to walk away from. -- D.F.H.[/i]
Contact a licensed agent at Fenner Insurance Agency, Inc. today for a no-obligation review of your current coverage. [url=/quote]Request your free quote online[/url] or telephone our office.

An umbrella policy sits above your automobile and homeowners policies and provides additional liability protection when the limits of those policies are exhausted. In today's litigious environment, a judgment can easily exceed the liability limits on a standard policy.

{{agency_name}} offers personal umbrella coverage in $1,000,000 increments. Speak with a licensed agent in {{city}}, {{state}} to learn whether an umbrella is right for your household.

blocks.text: An umbrella may be appropriate if you

items: Serve on the board of a non-profit organisation
Have a swimming pool, trampoline or dog
Have teenage drivers in the household
Have assets or future earnings worth protecting

blocks.body: The first million dollars of umbrella coverage is typically the least expensive coverage in your entire insurance program, often costing less per year than a single month of auto premium.

[i]This is the one page on this website I would keep. An umbrella is cheap, it is boring, and it is the only thing on here that has ever kept somebody in their house after a bad afternoon. We write about forty of them. -- D.F.H.[/i]
Contact a licensed agent at Fenner Insurance Agency, Inc. today for a no-obligation review of your current coverage. [url=/quote]Request your free quote online[/url] or telephone our office.

Your home is where your life happens. If you rent, your landlord's policy covers the building. It does not cover your belongings and it does not cover your liability to others.

{{agency_name}} can protect your personal property, your additional living expense if the unit becomes uninhabitable, and the dwelling coverage on your house against fire, wind, theft and vandalism.

items: Personal property, at replacement cost where available
Personal liability and medical payments to others
Loss of use and additional living expense
Protection for your home's foundation and attached structures
Scheduled items -- rings, guns, tools, instruments

blocks.body: The average renter in {{city}} owns between $20,000 and $30,000 of personal property, far more than most people estimate when asked. Renters coverage frequently costs less than $15 per month.

[i]The foundation line above is because this page is the homeowners page with the words changed, and whoever changed them missed one. We told Delbrook in October 2013 and again in 2014.

The coverage is real and it is about $140 a year and every student and every second-floor apartment on Bellamy Street should have it. -- B.K.[/i]
Contact a licensed agent at Fenner Insurance Agency, Inc. today for a no-obligation review of your current coverage. [url=/quote]Request your free quote online[/url] or telephone our office.

Flooding is the most common natural disaster and it is not covered by a standard homeowners policy. Flood insurance is written through the federal programme and is available to homeowners, renters and business owners.

As {{state}} enters hurricane season, {{agency_name}} encourages every property owner to review their exposure to storm surge and coastal flooding. There is a thirty day waiting period before a new flood policy takes effect, so waiting until a storm is named is waiting too long.

items: Building coverage to $250,000 on residential structures
Preferred risk policies outside the mapped floodplain
Excess flood above the federal limits

blocks.body: More than twenty per cent of flood claims come from properties outside the high risk flood zone, where a preferred risk policy is often available for a few hundred dollars per year.

[i]There is no storm surge in Verity County and there is no coastal anything. There is Kestrel Creek, and there is Tannery Flats in Gridfall, which is the mapped floodplain and which took four feet of water on 7 March 1994.

We write eleven flood policies in Tannery Flats. A county planning memorandum in 2005 estimated that about thirty properties down there had none, and I have no way of knowing whether that number is still right, and neither has anybody else. The [url=synth://wiki.gridfall.net/wiki/flood-1994]wiki write-up of the flood[/url] has the memorandum in it.

The thirty day wait is real and it is the part people find out about too late. -- D.F.H.[/i]
Contact a licensed agent at Fenner Insurance Agency, Inc. today for a no-obligation review of your current coverage. [url=/quote]Request your free quote online[/url] or telephone our office.

Weekends are what you work for. Whether you are towing a travel trailer, launching a boat, or riding the trails, {{agency_name}} can protect your recreational investment.

Many owners assume their auto policy extends to recreational vehicles. In most cases it does not, and in {{state}} the registration requirements differ by vehicle class.

items: Travel trailers, fifth wheels and motor homes
All terrain vehicles and side by sides

blocks.body: Coverage for a travel trailer should include liability for the period when the trailer is parked and being used as a residence, which is not automatically included on every policy.

[i]In this county this page means camper trailers, four-wheelers and about nine boats. Two of the boats are on the same road.

If you tow it on the road, your auto liability follows the trailer while it is hitched and does not cover the trailer itself. That is the thing people get wrong. -- T.F.[/i]

blocks.text: What we can and cannot do

blocks.body:
[b]We can:[/b] file the report for you, find your policy number, tell you what your deductible is, chase an adjuster who has not rung you back, read an estimate and tell you what is missing from it, and tell you honestly whether a claim is worth filing at all.

[b]We cannot:[/b] decide your claim, pay your claim, raise your limits after the fact, or add coverage to a policy after a loss. Nobody can do the last one and anybody who says they can is committing a crime and offering to make you a party to it.

[b]Ask us first on a small one.[/b] A $900 claim against a $1,000 deductible is a claim on your record for nothing. Ring and ask. It costs nothing to ask and we will tell you not to file it.

Food spoiled by a power failure is covered under most homeowners policies, usually to $500, and the deductible applies first. Photograph the freezer before you empty it and write a list with prices.

The June 2003 outage in Gridfall produced forty-one claims through this office over the following two weeks. Thirty-eight were freezers. The companies paid all but two, and the two were both policies with a $1,000 deductible and about $300 of meat in them. That is what usually happens and it is worth knowing before you spend a morning on it.
The [url=synth://ashkettlevfd.org/safety]Ashkettle fire company's safety page[/url] on chimneys and space heaters is better than anything we could write and we have handed it out at renewals.

[i]Nothing on this page is written by this office. The articles came with the website on a content subscription. The subscription was dropped in the summer of 2014 and the page stayed where it was. -- posted for D.F.H., 2018[/i]

blocks.text: Five Ways To Prevent a Kitchen Fire

blocks.body:
Cooking is the leading cause of home fires. Never leave a pan unattended on a lit burner. Keep dish towels, packaging and curtains away from the stove. Clean grease from the range hood regularly. Keep a lid nearby to smother a pan fire, and never carry a burning pan to the sink.

Install smoke alarms on every level of your home and test them monthly.

[i]Posted 17 June 2013. Provided by the Delbrook Content Service.[/i]

blocks.text: Is Your Teen Driver Ready? A Checklist for Parents

blocks.body:
Adding a teenage driver to your policy is a significant step. Establish rules about passengers, night driving and mobile telephone use before the keys change hands, and put them in writing. Many carriers offer a good student discount for a B average or better.

Talk to your agent before you purchase a vehicle for your teen. The vehicle you choose affects the premium more than most parents expect.

[i]Posted 1 July 2013. Provided by the Delbrook Content Service.[/i]

blocks.text: Back To School: Watch for Buses and Children

blocks.body:
School is back in session across {{city}} and the surrounding communities. Remember that it is illegal to pass a stopped school bus with its lights flashing in all fifty states. Slow down in school zones, watch for children stepping out between parked cars, and allow extra time in the morning.

The fifteen minutes you save is not worth what it could cost.

[i]Posted 12 August 2013. Provided by the Delbrook Content Service.[/i]

blocks.text: Hurricane Preparedness: Secure Your Property Before the Storm

blocks.body:
As the season peaks, property owners should review their preparations. Trim trees away from the structure, secure outdoor furniture, know your evacuation route, and photograph your possessions for your records. Remember that flood damage is not covered by a standard homeowners policy and that there is a thirty day waiting period on new flood policies.

Contact {{agency_name}} to review your coverage before a storm is named.

[i]Posted 3 September 2013. Provided by the Delbrook Content Service.[/i]

Autumn is the time to prepare your home for winter. Clean the gutters and downspouts, have the furnace serviced, inspect the roof for missing shingles, reverse ceiling fans, and have the chimney swept if you burn wood.

A chimney fire is among the most preventable of all home losses and among the most expensive when it is not prevented.

[i]Posted 30 September 2013. Provided by the Delbrook Content Service.[/i]

blocks.text: Deer Season: What To Do If You Hit One

blocks.body:
Deer are most active at dawn and dusk during the autumn rut. If a collision is unavoidable, brake firmly and do not swerve. Swerving is what turns a repairable front end into a roll-over.

Damage from striking an animal is covered under comprehensive rather than collision on most policies, which typically means a lower deductible. Report the collision and contact your agent.

[i]Posted 14 October 2013. Provided by the Delbrook Content Service.[/i]

blocks.text: Winter Driving: Slow Down and Leave Room

blocks.body:
Four wheel drive helps you go. It does not help you stop. Increase your following distance to eight or ten seconds on snow and ice, accelerate and brake gently, and keep the fuel tank above half.

Carry a blanket, a shovel, sand or cat litter, and a torch. If you slide off, stay with the vehicle.

[i]Posted 9 December 2013. Provided by the Delbrook Content Service.[/i]

blocks.text: Protect Your Identity After a Data Breach

blocks.body:
Review your statements monthly. Shred documents containing account numbers. Use different passwords for financial accounts and check your credit report annually, which you may do at no charge.

Many homeowners policies now offer identity restoration coverage as an endorsement for a small additional premium. Ask your agent at {{agency_phone}}.

[i]Posted 10 February 2014. Provided by the Delbrook Content Service.[/i]

blocks.text: Spring Thaw: Check Your Sump Pump Now

blocks.body:
Pour a bucket of water into the sump pit and confirm the pump switches on and the discharge runs clear of the foundation. Consider a battery backup; power failures and heavy rain arrive together.

Water that backs up through a sump or a drain is excluded under most homeowners policies unless sewer and drain backup coverage has been added.

[i]Posted 10 March 2014. Provided by the Delbrook Content Service.[/i]

blocks.text: Grilling Safety: Five Things To Check Before You Light

blocks.body:
Position the grill well away from the house, the deck rail and overhanging branches. Check the gas line for leaks with soapy water. Clean grease from the trays. Never add lighter fluid to a lit fire, and never leave the grill unattended.

July is the peak month for grill fires.

This page was not part of the website package. Marlene wrote most of it down over about three weeks in 2013 because she was answering the same eleven questions on the telephone every day, and then we put it up.

It is the only page on here anybody in this office has read twice.

blocks.text: Will my rate go up if I ring and ask a question?

blocks.body: No. Asking is free and it is not recorded anywhere. Filing a claim can affect your rate. Asking whether to file one cannot, and we would rather you ask.

blocks.text: Do I have to come in?

blocks.body: No. Most of this can be done on the telephone and we can post or email anything that needs a signature. People come in anyway and we like it, and there is coffee, and it is not very good coffee.

blocks.text: Does my homeowners policy cover the food in my freezer when the power goes out?

blocks.body:
Usually yes, usually to $500, and your deductible comes off first. So on a $1,000 deductible the answer is almost always no in practice.

We have a real number for this. The June 2003 outage in Gridfall put forty-one claims through this office in two weeks and thirty-eight of them were freezers. All but two were paid. The two that were not were both $1,000 deductibles.

Photograph the freezer before you empty it, and write the list while you are throwing it out and not a week later.

One other thing, since it comes up every time this is mentioned: the state commission report on that fire came out in November 2003, it is two pages long, and it does not say lightning. People have been saying lightning since the week it happened. It is in the [url=synth://wiki.gridfall.net/wiki/substation-fire-2003]wiki article[/url] with the wording.

blocks.text: Somebody rang me saying my auto policy had lapsed and asked for a card number.

blocks.body:
That was not us and it was not your company.

We do not telephone you for a card number. If you want to pay by card you ring us, on 744-1195, a number you looked up yourself and not one you were given on the call.

[i]Added April 2021: the current version of this uses a website called fenner-insurance-billing.click and a letter with our address on it. The letter is a good forgery apart from the telephone number. If you get one, bring it in, and do not use the [url=synth://fenner-insurance-billing.click/]address on it[/url]. -- D.F.H.[/i]

blocks.text: Can you write my house if it has knob and tube wiring / a wood stove / a fuse box / a roof that is twenty-five years old?

blocks.body:
Probably, at a price, with one of the two companies that still will. Tell us before we write it rather than after the inspection photographs come back, because the second way costs you a cancellation on your record.

A twenty-five year old roof is the most common reason a company will not take a house in this county now. That is a change from ten years ago and it is not going back.

blocks.text: Why is my farm policy more than my neighbour's?

blocks.body:
Usually one of four things: a grain bin he does not have, hired help, a pond with a dock, or a lower deductible you asked for in 1998 and forgot about.

Bring both declarations pages in and we will tell you which. If it is the fourth one we can fix it in ten minutes.
No, and we have not since 2014. Nobody in this office is qualified to advise you on it and we are not going to pretend otherwise. We will tell you who to ring.

For most companies, yes. Cheque, cash, money order, or a card with a fee that the company charges and we do not see a penny of.

We do not take payment for Ardent National or the state fund. Those go direct and there is nothing we can do about it, including on the last day.

blocks.text: The bank says my escrow is short and it is your fault.

blocks.body: It is occasionally our fault and usually the bank's, and either way we can sort it out in one telephone call if you bring the letter in. Bring the letter. Not a photograph of the letter on a telephone; the number we need is in small print.

Your policies do not stop. Your family rings us and we deal with it, and there is no hurry in the first week and there is no charge for any of it.

We have done this for a lot of people here and we are not bad at it.

Email: [b]mailto:office@fennerinsurance.com[/b]

That is the whole office, not a person. Bonnie reads it. It is checked once in the morning and once about three, and it is not the way to report a claim -- for that, see the [url=/claims]claim numbers[/url].

Bellamy Street, town side of the town hall, third door down from the corner of Fenn Avenue. Brick, white door, gold letters in the window. If you have reached the Alliance church on Rensbury you have gone two blocks too far.

Parking is behind, off the alley. Four spaces. The kerb is high and the second space is not as wide as it looks.

141 Mill Street, between the pharmacy and what was the hardware. It was Kerchner Jewelers until 2007 and there are people who still call it that when giving directions, including us.

Two days a week only, Monday and Thursday. There is a slot in the door for payments and it is emptied on those two days and not in between.

blocks.text: Privacy policy and terms of use

blocks.body: [i]Last revised: January 2011.[/i]

{{company_legal_name}} ("we", "us", "our") respects the privacy of visitors to this website (the "Site"). This policy describes the information we collect and how it is used. By using the Site you consent to the practices described in this policy.

We collect information you voluntarily provide through forms on the Site, including your name, address, telephone number, email address and details of your insurance needs. We may also collect non-identifying information such as browser type, referring page and the time of your visit, which is used in aggregate to improve the Site.
The Site uses cookies to remember your preferences. Most browsers permit you to refuse cookies. If you refuse cookies certain features of the Site may not function as intended.

We do not sell your information. We may share information with the insurance carriers we represent for the purpose of preparing a quotation, with service providers who operate the Site on our behalf, and where required by law or by the regulatory authorities of the State of {{state}}.

Residents of California may request a list of third parties to whom we have disclosed personal information for direct marketing purposes during the preceding calendar year. Requests should be directed to the address listed on the Contact page.

The content of the Site is provided for general informational purposes only and does not constitute an offer of insurance or a statement of coverage. No coverage is bound, altered or cancelled by any communication submitted through the Site. Coverage is subject to the terms, conditions and exclusions of the actual policy issued. In the event of a conflict between the Site and the policy, the policy governs.

The Site may contain links to third party websites. {{company_legal_name}} does not control and is not responsible for the content of those sites.
